findings.description: Image 00 (t=4.25s, Settled Act 1): Strong settled composition. ProtoType dominates center with a crisp blue accent border; all 3 corner subs (TL rhythm game, BL blue typography, TR anime characters) peek cleanly behind it. The 2x2 dock is neat and aligned, though the TL dock slot (FoldLayers) is near-solid black and reads almost empty at ~350px width. Minor dark-area WebP macroblocking in the radial background is acceptable.

Image 01 (t=5.50s, Mid-transition Act 1->2): Top-heavy transition layout with excessive dead space across the bottom third and lower-left as incoming rhythm game (upper-left, already holding the blue accent border) and outgoing ProtoType (upper-right) sit side-by-side, leaving the blue typography card floating isolated in lower-center dead space. Inside the dock plate, the incoming dimmed gray card overlaps ~70% directly on top of the teal thumbnail in the upper-right area while misaligned off-grid, leaving dock TL and BR empty. Faint dark rectangular WebP inter-frame ghost outlines are visible in the empty left background.

Image 02 (t=6.00s, Settled Act 2): Clean, well-balanced settled act. The yellow rhythm game commands center with crisp blue border and strong ~350px legibility; all 3 corner subs (TL FoldLayers, BL dark UI, TR ProtoType) and all 4 dock thumbnails sit neatly in place with zero overlap.

Image 03 (t=6.50s, Settled Act 2): Consistent hierarchy, crisp accent border tracking, lively motion in the protagonist, and spotless 2x2 dock neatness. High readability at ~350px with no visible artifacts or glitches.

Image 04 (t=10.00s, Early transition Act 2->3): Good causal main hand-off—outgoing rhythm game keeps the blue accent border in front while shifting slightly right as incoming FoldLayers/AE timeline expands from behind at TL. Minor clutter near the dock: a narrow sliver of the exiting dark anime card peeks tightly between the protagonist's bottom-right corner and the dock plate, while only 2 thumbnails remain in the dock (TL and BR) and the lower-left opens into noticeable dark dead space.

Image 05 (t=10.75s, Late transition Act 2->3): Main protagonist (AE timeline) has cleanly taken center and the blue accent border with outgoing rhythm game parked at TR. However, the dock exhibits a severe pileup and disappearing card: Dark UI stacks directly over ~60% of ProtoType in the top-left slot (pushing ProtoType against the plate's top rim), the gray glasses card sits off-grid near bottom-center, the entire right column of the dock is empty, and the 4th dock card (blue typography, re-slotting TL->BR) is completely invisible/occluded.

Image 06 (t=11.25s, Settled Act 3): Strong settled frame with high contrast and clear visual hierarchy. AE timeline protagonist ("But now") holds center with a crisp blue border; corner subs (TL pointing anime, BL teal anime, TR rhythm game) are well-balanced; 2x2 dock is completely neat and aligned. Minor note: both top-row dock thumbnails (ProtoType, Dark UI) are very dark at ~350px scale.

Image 07 (t=15.75s, Mid-transition Act 3->4): Causal main hand-off reads well (outgoing AE timeline keeps the blue accent border in front while incoming pointing-anime rises cleanly from behind at TL, with balanced canvas coverage). CRITICAL DOCK OCCLUSION BUG: at bottom-right, the incoming dock-bound yellow rhythm card is clipped behind the dock plate's top rim—roughly its lower 35% is hidden behind the plate's dark surface, reading unambiguously as a z-order glitch (card wrongly disappearing behind the dock tray) rather than intentional depth, despite revision 9's fix.

Image 08 (t=16.25s, Late transition Act 3->4): Pointing-anime protagonist has landed cleanly at center with crisp blue border and strong ~350px readability. Two issues: (1) inside the dock, the arriving teal anime card overlaps ~60% of the yellow rhythm card in the BL slot and protrudes past the slot edge while BR stays empty; (2) the TL sub (glasses anime) lands on a near-blank uniform gray frame that reads like an unloaded placeholder at 350px.

Image 09 (t=21.25s, Early transition Act 4->5): Protagonist remains full-size and dominant with crisp blue accent border. However, because the TL sub (glasses anime) is park-bound in Act 4->5 and begins its ~0.8s early shrink/departure, the entire top-left quadrant is already completely vacant dark space before the protagonist or TR sub move, breaking symmetry. At the dock, the exiting teal card sweeps straight across the occupied BL yellow card and juts halfway past the dock plate's left rim into the tight gap beside the protagonist.

Image 10 (t=21.75s, Mid-transition Act 4->5): Causal layering between main cards works (outgoing pointing-anime retains the blue border in front/upper-right while incoming blue/white grid card grows from behind at BL), but the upper-left quadrant forms a large ~25% empty black void (TL sub already departed behind the main pair while ProtoType hasn't arrived from the dock yet). FoldLayers floats small and isolated above the dock, the teal card peeks only as a tiny sliver beneath the protagonist, and the dock holds only 2 cards (TR, BL).

Image 11 (t=22.25s, Late transition / nearly settled Act 5): Striking, ultra-readable high-contrast blue/white protagonist ("夜 / Params") centered with blue accent border (the thin blue border has slightly reduced contrast against bright white/blue edges, though still legible) and all 3 corner subs settled cleanly. However, a trailing dock collision persists after the act has otherwise settled: the arriving glasses anime card still overlaps ~65% of the yellow rhythm card in the dock BL slot with BR empty.

Top Fix #1 (Highest Impact) — Fix z-order so travelling dock-bound cards NEVER clip behind the dock plate: In Image 07 (t=15.75s), the descending yellow card is visibly sliced behind the dock plate's top rim. Ensure the dock plate always renders strictly beneath all travelling/entering/exiting cards (only demoting strictly settled slot pairs, or never letting the plate itself occlude any card), eliminating the broken disappearance artifact.

Top Fix #2 — Eliminate dock slot-crossing pileups and trailing arrivals (Images 01, 05, 08, 09, 11): Stagger dock exits earlier than entries, shorten/ease-out arrival timing so all dock cards settle concurrently with the new protagonist (fixing Image 11's lingering overlap), and route horizontal/diagonal dock moves (such as TL->BR in Image 05 and BL-pass-throughs to/from BR in Images 08, 09, 11) with clean arc offsets or tighter re-slot choreography so cards don't stack over occupied slots or vanish mid-shuffle.

Top Fix #3 — Reduce mid-transition dead space and balance corner-to-dock departures (Images 01, 09, 10): In Act 1->2 (Image 01), keep outgoing/incoming main cards more vertically centered during cross-fade/handoff so the bottom third doesn't empty out. In Act 4->5 (Images 09-10), reduce or delay the ~0.8s early departure for TL-to-dock moves (or bring the incoming TL sub out of the dock earlier) so the upper-left quadrant doesn't sit completely blank for ~0.75s before and during the handoff.

verdict.summary: Verdict: ACCEPT WITH FIXES. Settled acts (Images 00, 02, 03, 06) are strong—protagonist dominance, blue accent border tracking, 2x2 dock neatness, and readability at ~350px are all solid, with no frozen/stretched frames and minimal WebP compression artifacts. Causal main hand-offs read cleanly in Acts 2->3, 3->4, and 4->5. However, revision 9 still has three clear transition defects: (1) a dock-plate z-order occlusion bug in Image 07 (t=15.75s) where the descending yellow card clips behind the dock plate's top rim; (2) recurring dock slot-crossing pileups and a vanished re-slotting card across Images 01, 05, 08, 09, and 11 (including trailing overlaps after Act 5 settles); and (3) noticeable mid-transition dead space in Image 01 (empty bottom third) and Images 09-10 (vacant upper-left from early TL park-bound departure). Top 3 fixes by impact: 1. Keep the dock plate strictly behind all travelling/entering/exiting cards so Image 07 never clips behind the plate rim. 2. Stagger dock exits/entries, finish dock arrivals in sync with protagonist settle, and add subtle arc/slot-routing separation to prevent dock pileups and disappearing re-slots (Images 01, 05, 08, 09, 11). 3. Rebalance Act 1->2 vertical staging (Image 01) and tighten TL-to-dock early-departure timing vs. incoming TL arrival in Act 4->5 (Images 09-10) to eliminate empty quadrant voids.
